messages.author: c78bfd9857351762
messages.subject: effective N calculations; warnings; BOLT LMM
parts:
To all,

I have 3 points to clarify with regard to common factor model with individual SNPs:

1.  I can run the effective N but don't I really need just N for downstream evaluation (e.g., MR).  I have 3 traits, with N1 = 173000 (N1cases - 59000), N2 = 550000 (N2 cases = 120000) and N3 = 450000 (N3 cases = 40000).  Effective N calculated to be 220000.  What would N, not effective N, be for common factor?  Sum of samples (excluding overlap, say with UKB cohorts used for different traits)?  

2. Running common factor, I received the LAVAAN negative variance warning for some of the SNPs (with fail = 0).  Should I exclude these SNPs?

3. On page or part 2 of the WIKI , you say that when using BOLT LMM GWASs (say the MRC IEU UKB pipeline GWASs): "Since BOLT-LMM controls for sample structure that would otherwise be captured by the LDSC univariate intercept, for BOLT-LMM traits it is most sensible to set the LDSC intercept to 1. For right now, this can be achieved by manually setting the diagonals of the intercept matrix (the third part of the LDSC output named I) for the traits analyzed using BOLT-LMM to 1."  Is this still advised (in an earlier response, PROF Tucker Drob advised against adjusting BOLT-LMM trait intercepts.  

Thanks for your advice.

Best, 
Dan

messages.author: d6d83e22ef3ba9f1
messages.subject: Re: effective N calculations; warnings; BOLT LMM
parts:
Hi Dan, 

Responses below: 
1. As long as you are using unit loading identification, you can calculate effective N directly from the summary statistics as is described at the bottom of the common factor GWAS wiki page (https://github.com/GenomicSEM/GenomicSEM/wiki/4.-Common-Factor-GWAS). There isn't an observed N for the factor, so my recommendation would be to use the average N implied by the summary statistics for any downstream analyses that require sample size. 

2. I would not interpret results when residuals are negative. Options in this case include determining which variable is producing a negative residual and putting a constraint on the residual to be above 0 or excluding those runs entirely if it's a very small subset of SNPs. 

3. My recommendation would be to set the intercepts to 1 for BOLT-LMM analyzed traits. That said, at the end of the day if you don't set the intercepts to 1 then you are producing slightly conservative results, which is generally fine to my mind. 

Best, 
  Andrew

messages.author: d6d83e22ef3ba9f1
messages.subject: Re: effective N calculations; warnings; BOLT LMM
parts:
Hi Dan, 

1. The equation listed on the github will produce a sample size for each SNP, and if you need to provide a total N to the external software I would take the average N across SNPs. 

2. It's often the case that the residual variance of the indicators is negative and not the factors, so that's one thing to keep in mind when trying to diagnose the issue. But I would recommend either excluding the SNPs with the warning if a small subset, or troubleshooting further if it's a larger set of SNPs. It sounds like in your next message it is a large set of SNPs so simply excluding those runs that produce this warning is not ideal. I see you've posted in a separate thread about this same issue so I'm going to respond to you their. 

3. Sounds good!

Best, 
  Andrew
